Four Elgin Community College students have been named Seigle Scholars and will receive funding that covers their tuition, fees and books for up to 60 credits toward an associate degree.

The 2026-27 recipients are Juliana Arroyo, of Hanover Park, a Bartlett High School graduate; Gianna Deutsch, of Elgin, a St. Edward Central Catholic High School graduate; Leah Foerster, of Elgin, an Elgin High School graduate; and Solis Jaime, of Carpentersville, a Hampshire High School graduate, a news release said.

Arroyo is majoring in nursing and has worked with patients during certified nursing assistant clinicals at a local rehabilitation center. Deutsch is studying business and volunteers with St. Patrick Parish Vacation Bible School and nonprofit Feed My Starving Children.

Foerster, a psychology student, has served as a dance captain and helped choreograph and teach performances. Jaime is pursuing an associate degree in liberal studies and has been active in Girl Scouts and various school organizations.

The Seigle Scholar program was established in 2024 by philanthropists Mark and Robin Seigle. This is the third group of scholars for the program.

Playground renovations at Shenandoah Park in Carpentersville are now complete and the area reopened to the public.

The park is at Alexandria Lane and Plantation Drive, just west of Sleepy Hollow Road and north of Huntley Road.

“You can see it across the open space as you drive on Sleepy Hollow Road,” Dundee Township Park District Executive Director Dave Peterson said.

In September, nonprofit Kids Around the World helped remove the old equipment and will repurpose it for children who are in need of a playground, according to a Dundee Township Park District social media post.

New equipment includes swings, slides, climbing structures and a spinner. Peterson said the project cost $150,000 and was paid for with money from the park district’s capital fund.

South Dakota-based nonprofit All Kids Bike has launched its Kindergarten PE Learn-to-Ride Program at Elgin Math and Science Academy through a $9,000 donation from the Minnesota-based Life Time Foundation.

The program includes teacher training and certification, an eight-lesson curriculum, 24 Strider balance-to-pedal bikes, pedal conversion kits, student helmets and an instructor bike.
